title.narrative: Output 7.3. Increased capacity of Member States to set adequate wages and promote decent working time

description.narrative: On 27 April 2023, the Mauritius Minimum Wage Consultative Council (MWCC), a tripartite commission acting on behalf of the Mauritius Ministry of Labour, Human Resource Development and Training of the Republic of Mauritius, presented the Fifth Report (2021/2022) on the impact of the implementation of the National Minimum Wage in the Republic of Mauritius – the ‘Fifth Impact report on the minimum wage in Mauritius’. The report considered the current economic conditions in the country, particularly the recent crises that have impacted in the economy (the COVID-19 pandemic, the cost-of-living crisis) and, as per the National Wage Consultative Act, the Chairman of the council stated that the next review of the minimum wage, in view of adjusting the level, will take place in January 2025. In June 2022 the Mauritius Minimum Wage Consultative Council (MWCC) requested the ILO to produce a study to assess the effect of recent crises (COVID-19 and the cost-of-living crisis) on the effective implementation of the minimum wage, where the latter was implemented in the country for the first time in January 2018. The objective of the study was to help the MWCC decide on the future adjustments of the minimum wage while considering the effect of the above mentioned crisis on the economy of Mauritius. The ILO produced a report that examined wages and wage outcomes in Mauritius using the quarterly survey known as the Continuous Multipurpose Household Survey, (CMPHS), from 2019Q1 to 2021Q4, as well as average monthly wage data up to the second quarter of 2022; the two sources of data were provided to ILO by Statistics Mauritius. Among other things, the empirical evidence in the report shows that during the harshest months of the COVID-19 pandemic, real monthly wages collapsed in Mauritius (alongside a collapse in wage employment), and although there was a gradual increase in employment during 2021 and 2022, real monthly wage growth declined by 1.9 per cent during the first two quarter of 2022, an outcome that was in line with global estimates and due to the cost-of-living crisis that impacted in most countries and regions from 2021. The estimates in the report also showed that between 2021 and 2022, and despite the nominal increase in the minimum wage, the two levels of minimum wages (for the non-exporting and for the exporting sector) declined in real terms by 4.4 percent and 4.7 percent for, respectively. The report concludes with a battery of recommendation to help the MWCC take action to continue with the effective implementation of the minimum wage system, as well as recommendations for the achievement of sustained and sustainable adequate wages for all.

title.narrative: The ILO’s Decent Work Results Dashboard

description.narrative: The ILO’s Decent Work Results Dashboard –complementing the ILO’s Programme Implementation Report – presents information on the results achieved and on the most significant outputs delivered by the ILO during the relevant biennium.

description.narrative: The ILO’s Results Framework is always part of the Programme and Budget (P&B) document for the relevant biennium. Please refer to the Annex “Results Framework” of the relevant P&B Document

The ILO’s biennial Programme Implementation Report is an instrument of accountability. It describes the performance of the Organization against the commitments made in the Programme and Budget documents for the corresponding biennial period.
